MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron has a weak, diffuse profile: it activates broadly across passages of technical/qualifying specification (product specs, rules, examples) and peaks on the function-word or unit token that introduces a concrete detail — e.g. " z" in German "z. B.", " for" in "See Description tab for details", " at" in "Action tag at the end", "g" after a weight — rather than on any consistent single surface form; it is suppressed on names, bare numerals and "the" in ordinary narrative/list text.

L10·N14137unmasked layer
This neuron has no clean semantic target: its top activations fall on ordinary function/continuation words immediately after a verb or in a fixed phrase ("rushed **to** the hospital", "figure out **what**", "hoped to **save**", "the world **over**", "Dear **Lord**", the comma closing an attributive "says X**,**"), while it is strongly suppressed by passive-voice auxiliaries/reporting verbs ("was", "were revealed", "believed to be") and opening curly quote marks — so it looks like a weak active-clause-continuation detector rather than a concept detector.
